title: First Receipted Human-in-the-Loop Critical Resolution in an Autonomous Self-Healing Infrastructure (N10-ACK)
description:

Abstract: On October 4, 2026, an autonomous self-healing infrastructure refused to remediate a critical-severity anomaly in a cryptographic flow until a named human operator acknowledged the event, then executed the remediation and closed the complete trail in a public append-only ledger within minutes of the event. This short paper documents the cycle and its evidence chain: to our knowledge, the first end-to-end human-in-the-loop critical-resolution cycle in a self-healing autonomous infrastructure recorded as a deterministic, publicly timestamped receipt trail rather than an asserted claim.

Full chain: detect → hold (Rule: no auto-heal in cryptographic flows) → constitutional check → PQC validation → human ACK → heal (22 s) → resolve.

Evidence of record: public append-only ledger — github.com/LLong2026/four-horsemen (entries 0009, 0010; commits 700ea1e, c1f43bb, ccf691a), with the milestone summary in the same repository (MILESTONE_HITL_N10_Critical_Receipt.md).

Disclosures: the anomaly was a synthetic chaos-injection probe (Night 10) on a simulated target (SIMZ corpus). No real tenant, customer, or live cryptographic operation was involved. The run was a disclosed manual recovery of a scheduled workflow whose spawned session lacked cross-app write access; prior nights N7–N9 are recorded as missed, not backfilled. Zero PII, credentials, wallet addresses, or transaction amounts persisted (redaction-at-ingestion rule held).
